summary: The newest screened arXiv slice was thin on direct heavy-ion collision measurements but useful for physics-AI and nuclear-QCD infrastructure. Key themes are self-supervised heavy-flavour representation learning at LHCb, machine-learning-informed quarkonium screening, reinforcement-learning search over SMEFT operator space, parameter-conditioned latent dynamics models, and reproducible pQCD dense-matter workflows with finite strange-quark mass.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2609.09275 is the strongest selected item: it gives a concrete self-supervised transformer workflow for LHCb heavy-flavour environments and checks anomaly-score behavior in both simulation and 2017 collision Open Data.

papers.title: MUSES workflows for pQCD constraints on dense matter with finite quark masses
papers.short_authors: Isabella Danhoni, Mateus Reinke Pelicer, Debora Mroczek, Yumu Yang, Mauricio Hippert, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler
papers.abstract: The paper implements NLO pQCD thermodynamics with finite strange-quark mass in the MUSES Calculation Engine, comparing conserved-charge basis prescriptions and their effects on dense-matter flavor composition and EoS priors.

papers.title: Bottomonium suppression with a machine-learning-informed Debye mass
papers.short_authors: Ajaharul Islam, Shibo Chen, Fu-Peng Li, Long-Gang Pang, Guang-You Qin
papers.abstract: An ML-informed Debye mass is inserted into a complex KSU heavy-quark potential and propagated through QTraj to compute Upsilon suppression observables in Pb-Pb collisions.

papers.title: "Transforming" LHCb: self-supervised maps of heavy-flavour decays
papers.abstract: A self-supervised transformer learns heavy-flavour decay environments from masked particle-identification and constituent-completion tasks, performs competitively with supervised models in simulated LHCb Open Data, and shows anomaly-score response in 2017 collision Open Data.

papers.title: Searching for New Physics with Reinforcement Learning
papers.short_authors: Jacky Kumar, Marianne Bouchard, David London
papers.abstract: The paper frames SMEFT operator selection for anomaly explanation as a reinforcement-learning problem and tests it on the CDF W-mass anomaly and a more complex multi-anomaly scenario.

papers.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
papers.short_authors: Andy Zeyi Liu, Haoran Sun, Lucas Baker, Randall Balestriero, John Sous
papers.abstract: SG-JEPA conditions latent rollouts on physics parameters and reports improved out-of-distribution prediction and control on simple dynamics and robotics benchmarks.

cautions.title: More QCD Masterclass Lectures on Jet Physics and Machine Learning
cautions.abstract: Lecture notes covering event metrics, anomaly detection, scaling laws, classification limits, and symmetry-respecting regression in QCD-motivated ML; useful pedagogically but not primarily a new research result.

cautions.title: Development and Validation of a Physics-Guided Machine Learning Extrapolation Framework Using a Classical Transient Diffusion Benchmark
cautions.short_authors: Ashutosh Yadav, Alok Dubey, Prodyut Ranjan Chakraborty, Harshal Akolekar
cautions.abstract: A physics-guided ML extrapolation framework is tested on a one-dimensional transient diffusion benchmark with analytic validation; relevance to complex HEP/nuclear inference remains unproven.
